decisions.wording: 'Reduced clinician-rated PTSD symptoms' becomes 'lowered clinician-rated PTSD symptom scores'. 'Most participants could tell their group and expectancy was not measured' becomes: in MAPP2, the only trial that asked, 94% and 75% identified their group; MAPP1 did not assess blinding; neither trial reports a measure of expectancy. Loss-of-diagnosis denominators named (completers in MAPP1; for MAPP1 'everyone randomized' is everyone dosed). 'No trial compares' limited to the sources read (the review's search keywords included MAPS); 'the trial reports give no outcome after 18 weeks' (the sponsor's cost model used 17 months of follow-up, known only second-hand). Magnitude: the printed d of 0.91 explained. Population: high suicide risk excluded in MAPP2 only. Plain text follows.
decisions.relation: reduces, kept: the comparison is randomized, so causal language about the assigned package (MDMA against placebo within the same therapy) is supported, as for other randomized claims at low certainty on the site; the doubt concerns measurement and what the contrast isolates, which the statement says, and MDMA's own contribution is the contested claim's question.
decisions.status: replicated by the same team, unchanged.
decisions.grade: moderate -> low: risk of bias two levels (very serious). Unblinding documented in MAPP2 and not assessed in MAPP1, a participant-reported outcome, no reported expectancy measure and no record of assessors' guesses, a bias that runs toward a larger difference, is shared by both trials (so their agreement does not reduce it) and cannot be sized, against differences of 8.9 and 11.9 points with lower limits of 4.1 and 6.3. Both second readers and the first reader's strict reading. Other domains unchanged; the single sponsor is carried by the status, not by a further level.

The month of the FDA decision is cited to Marseille & Mitchell (2025), who give it (citing CNN); the BMJ gives no date. Yes side: the 17-month follow-up used in the sponsor's cost model and its documented fall in health-care use (second-hand, no figures); the phase 2 trials with a low-dose comparator in which the review judged the blind maintained or partly maintained (one significant, one not; second-hand); MAPP2's sex imbalance, which favours placebo. Neither side: longer follow-up known only second-hand. Editors' reading: follows the new certainties (low for the comparison, moderate for common adverse events, very low overall); 'the two commentaries that welcomed the first trial'; the sponsor's cost analysis and MPLONG added to what is missing.
